description.value: Fair Harbour Marina & Campgrounds sits on the traditional territory of the Ka:'yu:'k't'h'/Che:k'tles7et'h' First Nations on the remote northwest coast of Vancouver Island, serving as the primary gateway to the Kyuquot area. The facility combines camping and cabin accommodation with a full marina offering moorage, a fuel dock, and a boat launch, alongside a convenience store. For touring cyclists venturing to this seldom-visited corner of Vancouver Island, it offers a rare combination of services in an otherwise roadless coastal wilderness.

address.value: #1 Fair Harbour Forest Service RD, Fair Harbour BC, V0P 2A0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website was successfully fetched and confirms the business is actively open ('WE ARE NOW OPEN FOR 2025 BOOKINGS!'). The site lists features explicitly: Cabins, Camping, Parking, Moorage, Fuel Dock, Convenience Store, Boat Launch, and WiFi. No cycling-specific amenities (hiker/biker sites, showers, laundry, etc.) are mentioned; the convenience store on-site supports a 'Food nearby' confirmation. The OSM record name uses the plural 'Campgrounds' while the website consistently uses the singular 'Campground', which is flagged as a minor discrepancy.
concerns: OSM record name uses plural 'Campgrounds' while the website consistently uses singular 'Campground' (Fair Harbour Marina and Campground).
OSM record has no tags, phone, or address populated — all contact details sourced solely from the website.
The fuel dock listed is a marine fuel dock for boats, not camping fuel for cyclists.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, open, publicly accessible marina and campground at a remote gateway location on Vancouver Island, confirmed active for 2025 with online bookings.
enrichment_extras.notes: WiFi is listed as an on-site feature on the website. The facility is located at the end of a long gravel forest service road and is a remote destination rather than a through-route stop for most cyclists.

wow_evidence: primary gateway to the Kyuquot area … rare combination of services in an otherwise roadless coastal wilderness
